topic: ICSE 10th Board Section A - Part 1: Multiple Choice Questions (Marks: 20)

questions.question: Which primitive numeric data type occupies exactly 2 bytes of memory in Java?
questions.explanation: In Java, 'short' is a 16-bit signed integer, occupying exactly 2 bytes.

questions.question: Which Character class method returns true if the specified character is an alphabetic letter?
questions.explanation: Character.isLetter(char ch) inspects whether the argument is a letter in the Unicode standard.

questions.question: Which keyword specifies that a class inherits fields and methods from another class?
questions.explanation: The 'extends' keyword establishes classical inheritance between a subclass and a superclass.

questions.question: What is the return type of the method Math.random()?
questions.explanation: Math.random() generates a pseudo-random floating-point value of type double in the range [0.0, 1.0).

questions.question: What is the result of Math.ceil(-6.1)?
questions.explanation: Math.ceil() returns the smallest double greater than or equal to the argument; -6.0 is greater than -6.1.

questions.question: What does the expression 37 % 5 evaluate to in Java?
questions.explanation: 37 divided by 5 equals 7 with a remainder of 2; the modulus operator '%' extracts the remainder.

questions.question: What will "FOUNDATION".indexOf('N') return?
questions.explanation: indexOf() searches from index 0: 'F'(0), 'O'(1), 'U'(2), 'N'(3). It returns the first match at index 3.

questions.question: What is the technical term for wrapping primitive data types into their object equivalents?
questions.explanation: Boxing (or Autoboxing) is the automated or manual conversion of primitive types into wrapper class objects.

questions.question: Which escape character represents a single quote within a character literal?
questions.explanation: The sequence '\'' escapes the single quotation mark inside char literals.

questions.question: What is returned by "CONCENTRATE".substring(3, 6)?
questions.explanation: substring(3, 6) extracts characters from index 3 up to index 5 ('C', 'E', 'N').

questions.question: Which of the following loops evaluates its conditional statement at the end of every cycle?
questions.explanation: The 'do-while' construct is an exit-controlled loop that tests conditions after loop body execution.

questions.question: What will Math.min(-0.0, 0.0) return according to Java floating-point specification?
questions.explanation: In IEEE 754 floating-point operations in Java, Math.min(-0.0, 0.0) considers -0.0 strictly smaller than 0.0.

questions.question: What is the result of casting character '0' to an int: (int)'0'?
questions.explanation: In ASCII and Unicode encoding, the numeric digit character '0' has decimal code 48.

questions.question: Which keyword causes an immediate termination of the current method and optionally returns a computed value?
questions.explanation: The 'return' statement exits the enclosing method immediately and passes execution back to the caller.

questions.question: What is the return type of the method Character.toLowerCase(char ch)?
questions.explanation: Character.toLowerCase() converts a single character to lowercase and returns it as a primitive char.

questions.question: What is the default initial element value in an uninitialized array of double primitives?
questions.explanation: Java initializes all elements of an unassigned double array to default 0.0.

questions.question: What is the result of the expression Math.round(-3.5f)?
questions.explanation: Math.round(-3.5f) evaluates (int)Math.floor(-3.5f + 0.5f) = (int)Math.floor(-3.0f) = -3.

questions.question: Which search algorithm requires array elements to be arranged in sequential ascending or descending order?
questions.explanation: Binary search divides intervals in half and operates properly only on pre-sorted arrays.

questions.question: Which operator is used to perform logical negation (NOT) on boolean expressions?
questions.explanation: The '!' operator flips boolean truth values (true becomes false, and vice versa).

questions.question: What does the method "Computer".endsWith("ter") evaluate to?
questions.explanation: endsWith() verifies whether a string concludes with the specified suffix, returning boolean true.

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this constant variable initialization:
options: Cannot increment or reassign a value to a final variable
final cannot be used with int
questions.answer: Cannot increment or reassign a value to a final variable
questions.explanation: Variables marked with 'final' are constants and reject any modification after initial assignment.

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this single-character assignment:
options: Single-character literals must be enclosed in single quotes ('*'), not double quotes
Asterisks are invalid characters in Java
questions.answer: Single-character literals must be enclosed in single quotes ('*'), not double quotes
questions.explanation: Double quotes denote String objects; primitive characters strictly mandate single quote delimiters.

questions.question: Identify the logical flaw in this loop intended to iterate 5 times:
options: i++ increments instead of decrementing, causing an infinite loop because i >= 1 remains true
questions.answer: i++ increments instead of decrementing, causing an infinite loop because i >= 1 remains true
questions.explanation: Incrementing 'i' causes it to remain continuously greater than or equal to 1, producing an infinite loop.

questions.question: Identify the library method error:
options: Index 7 causes a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException because indices range from 0 to 6
topic must be initialized with new
questions.answer: Index 7 causes a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException because indices range from 0 to 6
questions.explanation: "Science" contains 7 characters with valid indices 0 to 6; index 7 is out of bounds.

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this 1D array creation statement:
options: Array dimension capacity must be specified using square brackets [10], not parentheses (10)
buffer is an illegal array identifier
new int() is used for classes only
questions.answer: Array dimension capacity must be specified using square brackets [10], not parentheses (10)
questions.explanation: Array dimension sizing in Java strictly requires square brackets: new int[10].

questions.question: Identify the logical error in this absolute difference calculator:
questions.code_snippet:
int a = 4, b = 9;
int diff = (a > b) ? (b - a) : (a - b);
options: The expressions are inverted; both branches produce a negative result instead of a positive difference
questions.answer: The expressions are inverted; both branches produce a negative result instead of a positive difference
questions.explanation: If a > b, it should compute (a - b); if false, it should compute (b - a). The current code inverts both.

questions.question: Identify the library method error:
options: Method name must follow camelCase: parseDouble()
questions.answer: Method name must follow camelCase: parseDouble()
questions.explanation: Java methods are strictly case-sensitive; the Double wrapper class method is parseDouble() with a capital 'D'.

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this method signature:
questions.code_snippet: public void execute(int a, float b); { }
options: Semicolon (;) before the method body terminates the signature prematurely
float and int cannot be combined
questions.answer: Semicolon (;) before the method body terminates the signature prematurely
questions.explanation: A method header defining a concrete code body must not have a semicolon prior to the opening brace.
